tagline: Map one web app's surface in one view.
lore: The Beagle, a scent hound that works a trail to map exactly where its quarry has been — here it follows navi's WAS info plugins to lay out one web app's terrain.
problem: A WAS scan collects far more than findings: the sitemap the crawler found, the scan's telemetry, cookies, allowed methods, external links, a screenshot. That context is what tells you how an app is built and exposed — and it's buried in informational plugins nobody reads.
does: Point Beagle at a web app and it lays out the terrain from navi's WAS info plugins — sitemap, scan telemetry, target facts, screenshot, external URLs, cookies and allowed methods — plus the app's other informational and security findings. Every plugin opens its raw stored output, proof and request / response headers.

glance.caption: Beagle on one web app: its identity, the recon plugins (sitemap, telemetry, target facts, screenshot, external URLs, cookies, methods) and its security findings — each plugin one click from its raw output.
glance.note: Screenshot not included: the test lab has no WAS data.

capabilities: sitemap, scan telemetry, target facts, screenshot, external URLs, cookies and allowed methods from WAS info plugins.
each plugin's stored output, proof and request / response headers.
the app's non-informational findings, alongside the other info plugins.
a dashboard link (a severity, an OWASP category, a technology, stale scans) narrows the app list to that group.
by app or asset UUID, or the riskiest app by default.
how: Beagle reads the WAS apps and findings tables in your local navi.db and changes nothing. WAS data needs a Tenable WAS license and `navi config update was`.
who: AppSec engineers and pen testers scoping an app, and app owners who want to see what the scanner saw.
better: Arachne and Vizsla send you here; Argos is the same deep-dive for infrastructure assets.
cta: Put Beagle on an app's trail — it maps everywhere the scanner went.
